ledger.note: 1778: the counts of Reuss Elder Line are raised to princely rank. The Greiz counts 'were elevated to princely status in 1778'. The land was the counts' own, not taken from another state; the page names no predecessor and the date is the elevation, not a founding.
1848: the state is officially called the Principality of Reuss Elder Line. 'officially called the Principality of Reuss Elder Line' after 1848; infobox 'Principality of Reuss Elder Line (1848-1918)'.

region.text: the Elder Line's territory around Greiz (317 km2)

ledger.note: 1919: the Elder Line's territory is combined with the Junior Line's into the People's State of Reuss, which joins Thuringia in 1920. The infobox range ends 1918; the Elder Line itself 'died out in 1927'.

certainty.note: A fixed small territory of 317 km2 (a German Confederation, then German Empire state); the page gives no frontier text.

sources.title: Reuss Elder Line
sources.note: Princely rank 1778, official name after 1848, area 317 km2, population 72,000 in 1910, merger into the People's State of Reuss 1919 and Thuringia 1920.

notes: New dossier, a state Cliopatria lacks; the neighbour principality-of-reuss-gera (Younger Line) is another group's. One thin page: it gives no infobox start or end dates ('Established' and 'Disestablished' are empty, the unlabeled infobox ranges 1782-1833 and 1901-1918 are unexplained), no capital, and nothing on the Confederation of the Rhine, German Confederation or German Empire years. The start (1778) is the elevation to princely rank by the page's sentence; the state was a county before that, and the pre-1778 history (Reuss-Obergreiz) is not covered. The end 1919 is the People's State of Reuss; the infobox says 1918. Counterpart 'peoples-state-of-reuss' needs a dossier (slugify of People's State of Reuss) from another group; the Younger Line's Reuss-Gera dossier ends 1871 and is an eu-20-h row. The 'found' event names no counterpart because the page names no predecessor state.
